name: Amasa Lyman
role: Apostle who helped lead the 1847 westward companies
dateNote: He became an apostle on 20 August 1842; section 136 names him in January 1847.
importance: Section 124 names him a counselor in the presidency of the high priests at Nauvoo. Section 136 tells him and George A. Smith to organize a company for the journey west. He led wagon companies to the Salt Lake Valley in 1847–1848. He lost his apostleship in 1867 and was excommunicated in 1870.
connections: Lyman E. Johnson baptized him in 1832. In section 136 he works with George A. Smith.

sources.title: Amasa Mason Lyman, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 30 Mar. 1813, Lyman, New Hampshire; baptized 27 Apr. 1832; apostle 20 Aug. 1842; counselor in First Presidency 1843–1844; Winter Quarters 1846; deprived of apostleship 6 May 1867; excommunicated 12 May 1870; joined the Godbeite movement; died Fillmore, Utah (date 4 Feb. 1877 from citations). 124:136 checked in local text.
